question.text: What will be the last date for filing claims and objections in Delhi's SIR, as of November 27, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the option containing the last date for filing claims and objections in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of Delhi's electoral rolls, as specified in the most recent official schedule in force at 23:59 IST (18:29 UTC) on November 27, 2026. Only official documents dated on or before November 27, 2026 count: Election Commission of India (ECI) notifications, letters and press notes, Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Delhi notifications and press notes, and Delhi Gazette publications of such notifications; a revision dated November 26 or 27, 2026 counts even if it is uploaded later. The baseline is ECI notification No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol. II) dated October 29, 2026, published in the Delhi Gazette as entry SG-DL-E-31102026-277561 (https://gazettetracker.com/g/SG-DL-E-31102026-277561), which sets this last date as November 25, 2026; if no later revision of that date is issued on or before November 27, 2026, the question resolves to "November 25, 2026 or earlier (no further extension)". If a revision sets different last dates for different categories of claims or objections, the last date applicable to Form 6 claims filed by individual electors governs. A revised last date of, for example, December 9, 2026 would resolve to "December 5 – December 15, 2026". If the official documents cannot be retrieved, resolution uses [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print: "Last date for filing claims and objections" means the final day on which an elector may file a claim (Form 6, Form 6A) or an objection (Form 7) under the SIR claims-and-objections period, as stated in the governing schedule. A change limited to the house-to-house verification, to the distribution or submission of Annexure-A enumeration forms, or to the deadline for disposal of claims and objections does not change this date; only a change to the final date for filing claims and objections does. If more than one revision is dated on or before November 27, 2026, the latest-dated one governs. If the governing document extends the period but states no closing date, the question resolves to "December 16, 2026 or later".

# Delhi SIR: last date for filing claims and objections (research as of 2026-11-17)

**Bottom line:** No official document extending Delhi's November 25 deadline has turned up. On November 17 the ECI revised the SIR schedule for Telangana and reportedly for six other places, Delhi among them. I could not confirm whether that revision changes Delhi's filing date, and I could not see the official order.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-29/30: The gazette entry SG-DL-E-31102026-277561 is ECI notification No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol. II) dated October 29, republished by CEO Delhi as No. CEO/COE/102(21)/2023/267 on October 30. It extends the claims-and-objections period (originally August 31 to October 30) to **November 25, 2026**. The gazette text I saw gives no revised disposal date or final-roll date. Press reports give December 15 and December 22. [gazettetracker](https://gazettetracker.com/g/SG-DL-E-31102026-277561); [ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/delhi-sir-timelines-revised-claim-filing-till-nov-25-final-roll-on-dec-22/3085594/)
- 2026-11-17: ceodelhi.gov.in timed out, so I could not check CEO Delhi's notices directly. I found no later Delhi gazette entry or ECI press note.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. As far as I can find, November 25 is still the official filing deadline.
- One possible complication: the November 17 revision may give Delhi a re-enumeration window for voters marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD). In Telangana that window runs November 18-30, past Delhi's November 25 date. If Delhi gets the same window, it would count only as an Annexure-A form change under the fine print, so it would not move the filing date unless the Form 6/7 deadline is changed too.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-17: Telangana Today reports the ECI revised Telangana's schedule:
  - ASDD enumeration forms to be generated by November 18, distributed and collected November 18-30, and disposed of by December 10.
  - Disposal of claims and objections moved to December 15 (from November 26); final roll moved to December 22 (from November 30).
  - It says Andhra Pradesh, Delhi, Nagaland, Maharashtra, Haryana and Jharkhand were also revised, with December 15 and December 22 as common dates. Delhi already had those two dates, and the report gives no new Delhi filing date. [Telangana Today](https://telanganatoday.com/eci-extends-telangana-sir-deadline-to-december-15-final-voter-list-on-december-22); The Hindu story in the news feed (I could not open it)
- 2026-11-17: The Tribune says only 31,027 Form 6 applications came in between October 30 and November 15 (about 3.10 lakh in total). Officials said another extension "could not be ruled out" and that fresh distribution of enumeration forms was expected to start later this week. [Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/delhi/slow-pace-of-form-6-applications-under-delhi-sir-after-deadline-extension/); [Daily Jagran](https://www.thedailyjagran.com/india/news/delhi-sir-voter-list-revision-sees-sluggish-response-only-31027-form-6-applications-filed-since-extension-10336554)
- 2026-11-17: The Supreme Court asked the ECI to respond to the opposition's request to serve it 48 written questions on the SIR. [Deccan Herald](https://www.deccanherald.com/india/supreme-court-asks-election-commission-to-reply-on-oppositions-interrogatories-in-sir-case-4221389)
- 2026-11-16: Activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri accused the ECI of "flagrant non-compliance" with its November 6 re-inclusion directive (Hindustan Times, per the news feed; I could not open it). The same day, a petition was filed in the Supreme Court alleging "ghost" Form 7 objections in Mustafabad. [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/plea-in-sc-says-ghost-form-7s-haunt-mustafabad-constituency-during-delhi-sir/article71709358.ece)
- 2026-11-13: Officials said an extension of about two weeks was being considered, not yet approved, and would be "taken up for discussion in the next meeting and finalised." [Indian Panorama](https://www.theindianpanorama.news/delhi-may-extend-sir-deadline-by-2-weeks-giving-47-6-lakh-excluded-voters-another-chance/)
- 2026-11-05/06: CEO Delhi reported 2.96 lakh Form 6 applications received. [Punjab Kesari](https://english.punjabkesari.com/india/296-lakh-forms-6-received-so-far-delhi-ceo)

## 4. Base rates
- Delhi's filing deadline has been extended twice out of two chances so far: September 30 to October 30 (notified September 26) and October 30 to November 25 (notified October 29, the day after a Supreme Court hearing). The extensions were 30 and 26 days long, and each was notified 1-4 days before the deadline.
- Other states in this phase have had repeated revisions. Telangana's final roll moved October 12 → October 19 → November 9 → November 30 → December 22. Maharashtra's filing date moved from October 26 to November 13. [TNM](https://www.thenewsminute.com/telangana/sir-deadline-extended-in-andhra-telangana-delhi-and-three-other-states)
- A two-week extension, as reported, would land around December 9, inside the "December 5 - December 15" bucket.
- One limit on long extensions: the current disposal deadline is December 15 and the final roll is due December 22. Unless those dates also move, a filing date after December 15 is hard to fit in.
- In earlier SIRs (Bihar 2025), the ECI told the Supreme Court that claims could still be filed after the deadline without formally changing it. [Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/india/deadline-over-but-can-still-file-bihar-sir-claims-ec-tells-sc)

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket listings supplied relate to this question; they are cricket, football and unrelated markets. I found no prediction market or expert forecast on Delhi's SIR deadline.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around November 18 onward: fresh enumeration-form distribution in Delhi is expected to start, and the full Delhi details of the November 17 revision may be published.
- 2026-11-19: Supreme Court hearing on the Delhi SIR Form 6 dispute. The October 29 extension came the day after the previous hearing.
- 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-25: the window in which the earlier extensions were notified.
- 2026-11-25: current filing deadline. 2026-11-27: resolution cutoff (documents dated November 26-27 still count).

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. Resolution is set by official documents dated on or before November 27, 2026. Earlier extensions were notified 1-4 days before the deadline, so the decisive window is roughly November 21-27.

(b) **Status quo:** The last date for filing claims and objections stays November 25, 2026, with disposal by December 15 and the final roll on December 22. That resolves to "November 25, 2026 or earlier".

(c) **Base rates:**
- Delhi's filing deadline has been extended both times it came due: by 30 days (notified September 26) and by 26 days (notified October 29).
- Other states in this SIR phase have had repeated revisions. Telangana's final roll moved four times and Maharashtra's filing date moved once.
- A naive base rate therefore favours another extension, perhaps 60-70%.
- Extensions are getting harder to fit in, though. Disposal (December 15) and the final roll (December 22) appear fixed under the November 17 multi-state revision. That makes a filing date after mid-December unlikely unless those dates move too.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **November 12-13 (TOI, Tribune, Indian Panorama):** An extension of about two weeks was under consideration but not approved, to be finalised at the next meeting. Two weeks lands around December 9, inside "December 5 - December 15".
- **November 17 (Tribune):** Form 6 filings are slow, only 31,027 between October 30 and November 15. Officials said a further extension "could not be ruled out".
- **November 17 (Telangana Today):** The ECI revised schedules for seven places, Delhi included, with common dates of December 15 for disposal and December 22 for the final roll. Telangana got an ASDD re-enumeration window of November 18-30. Under the fine print, a Delhi window like that would not change the filing date, and it could stand in for a formal Form 6 extension. Alternatively, the filing date could be aligned with the window's end (about November 30), which falls in the second bucket.
- **Ongoing:** The Supreme Court is listed for November 19 and has said the ECI could be asked to extend the date. The last extension came the day after a hearing.
- **Precedent (Bihar 2025):** The ECI told the Supreme Court that claims could still be filed after the deadline without formally extending it. That supports the status quo option.

(e) **Unexpected outcome scenario:** On November 19 the Supreme Court pushes hard on the non-compliance allegations, and the ECI extends Delhi's filing date to late December. It also moves the final roll into January, which resolves to "December 16 or later". A second scenario: the ECI relies only on the Annexure-A window and makes no formal Form 6/7 extension, leaving November 25 in place despite the reported plans.

**Reasoning:** I start from a base rate of roughly 35% for no extension and 65% for some extension. The fixed December 15 and December 22 dates lower the chance of a long extension. They also leave room for the ASDD window to be the main remedy, which keeps meaningful weight on the status quo. The reported two-week plan and the alignment with the window's end both point to a moderate extension, split between "November 26 - December 4" and "December 5 - December 15". No prediction market covers this question.

(b) **Status quo:** The last date for filing claims and objections stays November 25, 2026, which resolves to "November 25, 2026 or earlier". Disposal is due December 15 and the final roll December 22.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Delhi's filing deadline has been extended both times it came up, by 30 and 26 days. Each extension was notified 1-4 days before the deadline then in force, and one came the day after a Supreme Court hearing.
- Other states in this phase have seen repeated schedule revisions.
- The constraint is different now. Disposal is fixed at December 15 and the final roll at December 22, and the November 17 revision apparently kept those as common dates for seven places. Unless those move, a long extension does not fit.
- In Bihar 2025 the ECI chose to say claims could still be filed after the deadline, without formally changing it.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **For an extension:**
  - On November 12-13, officials said an extension of about two weeks was under consideration, which points to around December 9.
  - On November 17, officials said another extension "could not be ruled out".
  - Fresh Annexure-A distribution had not started as of November 13. Telangana's re-enumeration window (ASDD forms) runs to November 30, and Delhi may get the same.
  - The Supreme Court hearing on November 19 could prompt an extension, and the court has already said it could ask for one.
- **Against an extension:**
  - The November 17 ECI revision that reportedly covered Delhi kept December 15 and December 22 and announced no new Delhi filing date. That suggests the ECI may use the Annexure-A window as the remedy. Under the fine print, a change to that window alone does not count.
  - Form 6 inflow is slow, only about 31,000 since October 30, which weakens the practical case for more time.
- **If an extension comes while the December 15 and December 22 dates hold:** a short one to November 30 or early December (the "November 26 - December 4" option) fits better than December 9. A two-week extension would probably require moving disposal too.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** The Supreme Court on November 19 directs a substantial extension, and the ECI moves the final roll into January. The filing date then lands on December 16 or later, or the order extends the period with no closing date stated.

**How far I moved:** The 2-of-2 extension record would suggest roughly 70% for an extension. I moved down to about 63% because the November 17 revision may be the ECI's chosen vehicle and it left Delhi's filing date apparently unchanged. I split the extension probability between short extensions, which fit the fixed December 15 and December 22 dates, and the reported two-week extension, which fits only if disposal moves.
